title: Why Tibo is doubling down on SuperX: building the X growth tool he needed himself
summary: Tibo explains why he bought out SuperX's co-founder, spent six months in stealth rebuilding it, and bet on X over LinkedIn after selling Tweet Hunter and Taplio. He argues growth on X needs good content plus a small circle of supportive friends, and that building for your own need produces a useful product.

principles.text: Growth on X rests on two things: good content and a support network of friends.
principles.quote:
The current SuperX product comes from realizing what you need to grow on X:

- Good content

- Friends (your support network)

principles.text: Seed growth with about 10 highly supportive people who engage with everything you post.
principles.quote: You need a foundation of 10 incredibly supportive people who will like and engage with everything you do.

principles.text: Build something you desperately need yourself; daily personal use validates the product.
principles.quote:
The product works. The foundations are solid. I'm using it daily and seeing results.

This is what happens when you build something you desperately need yourself.

principles.text: Slow shipping of basic features is a competitive weakness; rivals who ship in days win users.
principles.quote: When X launched long-form posts, Tweet Hunter took multiple months to implement it. Competitors had it in days.

principles.text: A browser extension alone limits growth; a full web app is needed to scale.
principles.quote: We built the extension and it was quite successful. But I felt like it was hard to grow with just a Twitter extension. We needed a web app.

principles.text: When foundations are weak, accept a full revamp and work in stealth rather than rushing out a weak product.
principles.quote:
But we realized some foundations weren't there. We needed a complete revamp.

So we worked in stealth mode for 6 months.
